short: Conqueror of Rus' and Hungary, and founder of the khanate that ruled Russia for 250 years.
full:
Batu was a son of Jochi, Genghis Khan's eldest, and inherited the westernmost Mongol lands in 1227 — territory that, by Mongol custom, extended as far west as Mongol hooves could reach. In 1235 a kurultai granted him an army for that purpose, with Subutai as its effective commander. Over the next seven years he destroyed the principalities of Rus', broke Hungary at Mohi and sent raiding columns to the Adriatic.

News of Ögedei's death in December 1241 took the campaign home, and Batu never returned to Europe. He quarrelled bitterly with Güyük, who was marching against him when he died in 1248, and afterwards became the empire's kingmaker: it was Batu's backing that put Möngke on the throne in 1251. From his camp on the lower Volga, later fixed at Sarai, he summoned Rus' princes to be confirmed in their titles and to pay tribute. He died in 1255, having founded the state Russian chroniclers would call the Golden Horde.
